title: Recommendations for marathon runners: on the application of recommender systems and machine learning to support recreational marathon runners
authors: Smyth B, Lawlor A, Berndsen J, Feely C, Cunningham P
population: Position paper with case studies using fitness-app, smartwatch and wearable activity data from marathon runners
findings: Argues that the complexity of marathon training plus availability of real-time activity data provides an opportunity for machine learning and recommender systems to support runners as they train, race and recover.
Presents a mix of original and recent case studies illustrating what can be done with activity data routinely collected by mobile apps, smartwatches and wearables.
limitations: Abstract is a position statement with case studies and gives no numeric results; author list beyond the first three (Smyth, Lawlor, Berndsen) is from memory and not Crossref-checked; Crossref issued 2021-08-18 online.
implications: Supports the design pattern of continuously refreshed, data-driven prediction and recommendation from routinely collected activity data, but supplies no numeric parameters.
